title: Check that time limits can be adjusted
user_impact: If a time limit cannot be adjusted, users who need more time are cut off and may lose what they entered.
technical_impact: The page has form fields or a <meta http-equiv="refresh">, so a time limit is conceivable; time limits set by JavaScript (setTimeout, setInterval, session expiry) are not visible in the markup, so the page gets one manual-check note that users must be able to turn such a limit off, adjust or extend it; the delay of a <meta http-equiv="refresh"> is judged separately.

checks.applicability: Pages with form fields (input other than hidden/submit/button/reset, select, textarea) or a meta refresh.
checks.expectation:
One needs_review (UNTESTED) note per page, at the root, when the page has
form fields or a meta refresh; never pass or violation. The meta refresh
itself is judged by timing/meta-refresh. Pages without either get no note.
The checklist reads rendered elements only, so with layout styles a meta
refresh in the head alone (no fields) does not raise the note.
checks.manual_reason: Script-driven time limits (setTimeout, setInterval, session expiry) and whether users can turn them off, adjust or extend them are not visible in the markup; the document only shows that fields or an automatic refresh make a time limit conceivable.
